title: Design System: shrten Dispatch Label and Ledger

display.purpose: Oversized homepage promise in the condensed Antonio face.

auth-display.purpose: Large, narrow account proposition on the context side of an access document.

status-title.purpose: Oversized expired or missing-route headline inside a terminal document.

page-title.purpose: Dashboard, analytics, team, and workspace document headers.

ticket-title.purpose: Access, protected-link, route-status, dialog, and ledger-panel headings.

metric.purpose: Cobalt values in ruled semantic summaries and stat strips.

action.purpose: The joined, high-commitment homepage shorten control.

body.purpose: Tables, explanations, descriptions, and secondary content in Outfit.

label.purpose: Public fields, disclosures, URLs, and result state.

code.purpose: Uppercase route, access, page, and summary labels.

index-label.purpose: Sidebar group labels and the persistent ledger marker.

micro.purpose: Keycaps, table headings, badges, footer metadata, compact tags, and copy actions.

narrative.overview:
shrten treats a URL as a dispatched item with a traceable operational life. The public Dispatch Label remains the first expression: a long destination enters through one broad intake field and leaves as a compact link ready to hand off. The Dispatch Ledger extends that same physical language through access, management, analytics, collaboration, and route resolution without asking users to learn a second interface.

Warm thermal stock and carbon rules make the system tactile without making it ornamental. Safety orange marks the one action that commits the current workflow, while cobalt behaves like registration ink for routes, selected state, keyboard focus, metrics, and completed handoffs. Antonio carries promises, titles, and high-signal figures; Outfit carries readable product content; monospace labels expose operational structure.

The system is flat, square, and task-dense. Public perforation belongs to a real intake-to-handoff seam, auth becomes a ruled access ticket, signed-in work uses a persistent dispatch index plus dense ledger, analytics preserves the same compact reading order, and terminal routes become status documents. The metaphor clarifies the work and never changes the product's behavior.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, lightly mottled thermal paper in light mode and near-black stock in dark mode.
Carbon-black structure, cobalt registration cues, and one safety-orange commitment action per surface.
Antonio display and metric roles, Outfit body copy, and monospace operational labels.
Square controls, ruled headers, semantic summaries, dense ledger rows, and flat document overlays.
Restrained perforation only where access, routing, or handoff creates a real seam.
One operating language from anonymous shortening through account work and recipient status.

rules.name: The One Orange Action Rule
rules.body: Safety orange marks the highest-commitment action in the current surface; when an auth or route-status action becomes orange, the public navbar entry is demoted to carbon ink so two orange commitments never compete.

rules.name: The Blue Routing Rule
rules.body: Cobalt marks direction, registration, selected state, keyboard focus, data, or a completed handoff; it does not compete with orange for commitment priority.

rules.name: The Quantitative Gradient Exception
rules.body: Decorative gradients are absent; a continuous cobalt scale is allowed only when it encodes quantitative analytics, such as the country-map legend.

rules.name: The Three-Voice Rule
rules.body: Antonio persuades and announces, monospace operates, and Outfit explains; never introduce a fourth typographic voice without a product-level reason.

rules.name: The Ledger Density Rule
rules.body: Dense does not mean tiny: use the compact monospace roles for labels and metadata, keep data values and actions legible, and let rules—not reduced type—create structure.

rules.name: The Carbon Rule
rules.body: Resting hierarchy comes from one-pixel ink rules, perforations, and tonal stock—not ambient drop shadows, blurred glows, or glass panels.

rules.name: The Overlay Exception Rule
rules.body: Shadow may distinguish a temporary modal or mobile sheet from the document below; it must disappear when the overlay closes and must not migrate onto ordinary cards.

rules.name: The Square Control Rule
rules.body: Inputs and action buttons meet their ledger geometry with zero radius; rounding them into pills or soft cards breaks the dispatch metaphor and weakens the operational hierarchy.

rules.name: The Real Handoff Rule
rules.body: Use perforation only where the workflow crosses access, routing, issuance, or terminal resolution; ordinary grouping uses carbon rules.

rules.name: The Motion Has a Job Rule
rules.body: Movement may show travel, access, progress, selection, or confirmation; if it does not explain one of those states, keep the printed surface still.

rules.name: The Behavior Lock Rule
rules.body: Visual extensions may rearrange presentation responsively, but they must not change shortening rules, API contracts, persistence, permissions, account requirements, authentication behavior, or navigation destinations.

dos: Do make each operating sequence read left-to-right or top-to-bottom: intake, optional routing, commitment, result, and next action.
Do use orange for one decisive commitment and cobalt for routing, selected state, focus, data, or completed handoff.
Do preserve the paper texture's source provenance and native 334px × 376px repeat when reusing the shipping plate.
Do start management surfaces with a ruled document header, semantic summaries where totals matter, and task-dense ledger content.
Do preserve every row field and action when a desktop table becomes a mobile record.
Do use access and status ticket perforation only at real handoffs; use ordinary carbon rules for ledger grouping.
Do verify extensions in light and dark themes, at desktop and narrow mobile widths, with keyboard focus and reduced motion.
donts: Don't turn the public task, auth, status, or management work into centered rounded hero cards, floating glass panels, or a grid of generic dashboard cards.
Don't show two orange actions on one surface; demote the public navbar entry when auth or route recovery owns the commitment.
Don't use cobalt as a competing primary action or apply data gradients as decoration.
Don't add ambient shadows, oversized radii, decorative pills, or unrelated industrial marks to imitate the aesthetic.
Don't promote public perforations into ordinary dashboard regions; carry hierarchy, rules, type, and interaction behavior first.
Don't hide advanced options, copy feedback, theme choice, account navigation, filters, row actions, analytics ranges, or team permissions to simplify a narrow layout.
Don't claim that source-level completion proves authenticated rendered behavior; authenticated surfaces still require their own runtime acceptance evidence.
